reasoning: The claim that Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short at around 5 feet 2 inches is a historical myth caused by a confusion between French and English measurement systems, alongside British war propaganda. At his death, Napoleon measured 5 feet 2 inches in contemporary French units (*pouces*), which translates to approximately 5 feet 6.5 inches (1.68–1.70 meters) in modern/English standard units. This was average or slightly above average height for a French man during the early 19th century.
